report_name: Millions of California Students' Data Exposed in Testing Provider Breach

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Actor
threat_actors.description: An unidentified threat actor who gained access to the Educational Testing Service (ETS) systems using a compromised login credential between May and September 2026 and exfiltrated data of millions of California students.
threat_actors.goals: Data theft of student PII for potential identity theft or fraud.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The initial and primary attack vector was the use of a legitimate, but compromised, login credential to access the ETS site.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor accessed and copied files containing student information from an accessible file repository or database within the ETS environment.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
attack_patterns.description: The copied files containing student data were exfiltrated from the ETS environment to an attacker-controlled location.

identities.name: ETS (Educational Testing Service)
identities.description: California's standardized testing provider whose systems were compromised via a stolen login credential, leading to the exposure of millions of student records.

identities.name: California public school students
identities.description: The population of current and former students whose personal information, including names, addresses, and disability records, was exposed in the breach.

identities.name: California Department of Education
identities.description: Government agency that announced the data breach at its testing provider, ETS.
